title: kv-cache: adaptive memory rebalancing and eviction-priority for spillover/paging fragmentation
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and page-spillover scenarios were causing elevated GPU memory pressure and suboptimal eviction choices under mixed-sequence workloads. This produced increased latency variance and higher token-cost for tail requests in Dedicated clusters. This change introduces an adaptive memory rebalancing layer and eviction-priority scoring that reduces fragmentation, avoids unnecessary paging/spillover, and preserves hot prefix entries across batch windows.

What I changed (summary):
- Add adaptive mem-rebalance manager that periodically analyzes allocation fragmentation and issues in-place compaction or targeted migrations to host spill regions when beneficial.
- New eviction-priority scoring function that combines recency, per-token weight (sequence length), KV fragment co-location score, and spill_cost_estimate to prefer evicting cold fragmented shards first.
- Introduced a lightweight paging budget allocator to limit simultaneous spill I/O and avoid throughput collapse during compaction runs.
- Continuous-batching integration: the rebalance manager schedules compaction/migration work in priority windows that avoid high-throughput batching intervals.
- Exposed config knobs: kv.rebalance.interval_ms, kv.rebalance.threshold_fragmentation, kv.eviction.alpha_recency, kv.eviction.beta_fragment_cohesion, kv.paging.concurrent_limit.
- Added metrics and tracing: kv.rebalance.runs_total, kv.rebalance.last_duration_ms, kv.eviction.score_histogram, kv.paging.active_spills, and tracing spans for rebalance->migrate->evict.

Implementation notes:
- The manager runs lazily when fragmentation > threshold and GPU utilization < 70% (configurable) to avoid impacting hot inference traffic.
- Compaction is implemented via a lock-free defragmentation path for small fragments and a migration path for larger shards (move to a staging buffer then swap pointers).
- Eviction scoring is designed to be monotonic and stable across short-timescale scoring noise to avoid oscillation. We use an exponentially-weighted recency term plus a fragmentation penalty.
- Paging spill operations are limited by kv.paging.concurrent_limit to prevent I/O saturation; when the limit is reached, the system prefers eviction within-device over additional spills.

Tests and validation:
- Unit tests for scoring function, concurrent rebalance/migration, and paging budget enforcement.
- Integration tests using the perf-canary harness to validate throughput/latency impact under mixed short/long sequence workloads.
- Benchmarks on c5-gpu clusters (P4/P40 equivalent test rigs): median latency unchanged, p99 latency reduced by ~18% on mixed workloads; host spill I/O decreased by ~32% during sustained traces.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind kv.rebalance.enabled=false by default. Canary rollout to 10% of dedicated clusters -> monitor kv.* metrics and per-route p99s -> expand to 50% -> full.

Docs: runtime/kv_cache.md updated with design and tuning knobs; added a short recipe to tune kv.paging.concurrent_limit for storage-backed spill.

Related: linear tasks ENG-2741 (memory rebalancer MVP), ENG-2789 (eviction scoring design).

comments: Miguel Torres: Nice work - the fragmentation estimator looks promising. A few questions: 1) Can we avoid full-migration for shards < 4KB by coalescing? 2) How does this interact with the kv-cache eviction tracing we already ship?

Aisha Patel: Good points. For (1) we coalesce in-place for <4KB fragments via the defrag fast-path, which I added as compaction.rs::coalesce_small(). For (2) we emit stable spans and map the eviction.reason label to the existing tracing schema so dashboards keep working.
Sofie Nguyen: CI flagged a flaky test in compaction where concurrent inference can race with migration. Please add a stress test and consider an optional jitter backoff.
Aisha Patel: Added stress test compaction_race_test and introduced a 1-5ms jitter on scheduling when high-concurrency mode is detected. Test is in runtime/kv_cache/compaction_tests.rs.
Liam O'Connor: What guardrails are in place to prevent the rebalance work from impacting latency SLOs in production? Consider a preemption token tied to the request scheduler.

Aisha Patel: The manager checks GPU util and active batch windows and yields if util > configurable threshold. I also added a preemption hook that cancels compaction if any high-priority request arrives; details are in rebalance_manager.rs (preemptible_worklet).

merge_commit_message:
squash: kv-cache adaptive rebalancing and eviction-priority

Implements adaptive rebalancing across GPU device memory, improved eviction heuristics to reduce fragmentation and paging, and a paging budget to avoid I/O saturation. Includes metrics, tracing, tests, and docs.
release_notes: Added adaptive KV-cache memory rebalancing and eviction-priority scoring to reduce fragmentation and host spill I/O under mixed workloads. Feature is gated and off by default; see runtime/kv_cache.md for tuning guidance.
perf_summary: Perf-canary results: p99 latency reduced ~18% on mixed short/long sequence workloads; host spill I/O reduced ~32%; median latency neutral. No regression on short-only workloads. Metrics: kv.rebalance.runs_total and kv.eviction.score_histogram added.
